thread:
anya: Quick follow-up on the AcmeCorp dedicated pool outage last night. Root cause is peering + on-prem routing mismatch. Postmortem is live: <https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pc-2025-01-acme|pc-2025-01-acme>.
incident-bot: postmortem published by @anya — link above.
mike: ack. Which action items are still open?
anya: Open items I'm tracking now:
- ACTION-231: network remediation (owner: @mike)
- ACTION-232: on-prem checklist & runbook update (owner: @janet)
- ACTION-233: monitoring/automated route health (owner: @kevin)
janet: quick Q — the on-prem side was NAT + stale routes? want the exact failure mode before I edit the checklist.
rohith: short answer: asymmetric routing from a misconfigured peering policy + BGP community stripping on the customer's edge. Packets left via peering but return path went via on-prem NAT, so KV cache replication timed out.
kevin: low-risk mitigation we can push: add a short-lived proxy healthcheck in the dedicated pool to surface route flaps earlier, and a circuit-breaker to cut traffic to affected nodes. Can stage this.
mike: I can own the network remediation. Target full fix + rollout by 2025-02-03. Will coordinate with SRE for canary.
janet: I'll update the runbook and add an "on-prem peering sanity" checklist. @anya paste the checklist here and I'll convert to playbook steps.
anya: pasted checklist below (please edit):
```
- Verify BGP neighbor sessions and advertised prefixes (on-prem and cloud side)
- Confirm BGP community handling and no stripping rules
- Validate return path symmetry with traceroutes from multiple subnets
- Ensure on-prem NAT rules do not rewrite peer-to-peer traffic
- Validate KV cache replication under asymmetric path (test harness)
- Post-change: run smoke traffic through canary pool, monitor 1m latency and error spike thresholds
```
janet: :thumbsup: I'll turn that into step-by-step commands for customer edge. Do we want this appended to the peering runbook or a separate KB?
anya: append to peering runbook and create a concise KB for customers with minimum on-prem config. Tracking in Jira epic INF-4567.
rohith: note — this asymmetric-return pattern has appeared in two other Dedicated customers in the last 6 months. Recommend quarterly "peering audit" for Dedicated on-prem customers and add a test that simulates return-path asymmetry.
kevin: adding automated route-health alarms to dedicated monitoring. I'll create an alert (route-flap-rate > 5/min) and wire to eng-sre oncall.
mike: summary of commitments: network fix + canary by 2025-02-03, runbook update by 2025-01-20, monitoring in place by 2025-01-31. I'll add the milestone to INF-4567 today.
anya: thanks — I'll update the postmortem with owners, deadlines, and INF-4567 link. Weekly status check-ins on Tuesdays; I'll ping with progress notes. If anyone needs a temp owner swap, shout here.
kevin: noted, will open alert PR this week.
janet: draft KB by Friday, will share here for review.
mike: sounds good.
anya: closing thread for now — will reopen when postmortem is updated. :wave:
